incidente.resumo: An issue with a new control plane configuration rollout reduced capacity for low-priority traffic in Google's internal backbone network, causing elevated latency and errors for Cloud Networking, Cloud Storage and BigQuery in several regions; high-priority user-facing traffic was not affected. Engineers pushed a halt that paused new rollout actions (actions in progress continued) and, after a first rollback configuration push failed to reach all nodes, updated the configuration correctly by 12:40 US/Pacific, and services were restored by 15:02.

descricao.texto: At approximately 02:00 US/Pacific on 15 July, as an in-progress rollout expanded to more regions, Google engineers observed performance degradation in Cloud Networking due to reduced capacity.
trechos: At approximately 02:00 US/Pacific on Friday, 15 July, as an in-progress rollout expanded to more regions, Google engineers observed performance degradation in Cloud Networking due to reduced capacity.

descricao.texto: An issue with a new control plane configuration rollout caused a capacity reduction for low-priority classified traffic in Google's internal backbone network connecting data centers; constrained traffic in certain cloud zones affected the performance of some Cloud services.
trechos: The root cause was identified as an issue with a new control plane configuration rollout, causing low-priority classified traffic capacity reduction in Google’s internal backbone network connecting data centers.
During the period of the rollout and subsequent rollback, constrained traffic in certain cloud zones affected the performance of some Cloud services.

fatores_contribuintes.texto: Halting the rollout paused new actions, but actions already in progress continued and further reduced network capacity.
trechos: While this effort succeeded in pausing any new actions, those already in progress continued, which further reduced network capacity.

fatores_contribuintes.texto: Mitigation was slowed by the capacity reduction itself: engineering teams needed more than their usual time to safely undo the configuration change, and the first rollback configuration push was not applied to all nodes, due in part to the reduced network performance.
trechos: Mitigation efforts were slowed by the capacity reduction, and engineering teams required more than their usual time to safely undo the configuration change.
Their first attempt to mitigate using a configuration push was applied at 08:40 US/Pacific, but it was not successfully applied to all nodes, due in part to the reduced network performance.

descricao.texto: A new control plane configuration rollout for Google's internal backbone network; the summary says the issue was encountered during a combination of repair work and a routine network software upgrade rollout.
trechos: The root cause was identified as an issue with a new control plane configuration rollout, causing low-priority classified traffic capacity reduction in Google’s internal backbone network connecting data centers.
This service disruption resulted from an issue encountered during a combination of repair work and a routine network software upgrade rollout.

passos.texto: At 03:50 US/Pacific, engineers pushed a first mitigation to halt the ongoing rollout; it paused new actions, but actions already in progress continued.
trechos: At 03:50 US/Pacific, Google engineers pushed the first mitigation attempt to halt the ongoing rollout.
While this effort succeeded in pausing any new actions, those already in progress continued, which further reduced network capacity.

passos.texto: Engineers shifted to a global rollback of the problematic configuration; a first configuration push at 08:40 US/Pacific was not successfully applied to all nodes.
trechos: Subsequently, the engineering team shifted their mitigation efforts toward a global rollback of the problematic configuration.
Their first attempt to mitigate using a configuration push was applied at 08:40 US/Pacific, but it was not successfully applied to all nodes, due in part to the reduced network performance.

passos.texto: Engineers worked through alternate mitigations, and by 12:40 US/Pacific the configuration was updated correctly, which mitigated the majority of impact; by 15:02 US/Pacific services for all customers had been restored.
trechos: Google engineers worked through alternate mitigations, and by 12:40 US/Pacific, the configuration was updated correctly, and this mitigated the majority of impact.
By 15:02 US/Pacific on 15 July 2022, services for all customers had been restored.

acoes.texto: In progress: improve signals to detect significant changes in traffic for upgraded domains in the backbone network.
trechos: Google is committed to preventing future recurrence, and we are taking the following actions:
Improve signals to detect significant changes in traffic for upgraded domains in the backbone network.

acoes.texto: In progress: improve dashboards that help debug global- and domain-level control failures and configuration status.
trechos: Google is committed to preventing future recurrence, and we are taking the following actions:
Improve dashboards that help debugging global- and domain-level control failures and configuration status.

acoes.texto: In progress: improve the automated handling of disconnected local Software Defined Networking (SDN) controllers to reduce overall impact and mitigation time.
trechos: Google is committed to preventing future recurrence, and we are taking the following actions:
Improve the automated handling of disconnected local Software Defined Networking (SDN) controllers that will reduce overall impact and mitigation time.

acoes.texto: In progress: improve the global safety systems that globally halt elective rollouts on Google's wide area (WAN) networks when global capacity is reduced.
trechos: Google is committed to preventing future recurrence, and we are taking the following actions:
Improve the global safety systems that globally halt elective rollouts on Google’s wide area (WAN) networks, when global capacity is reduced.

acoes.texto: In progress: further isolate production network neighborhoods.
trechos: Google is committed to preventing future recurrence, and we are taking the following actions:
Further isolate production network neighborhoods.

acoes.texto: In progress: improve the API to push changes to global and local network controllers during a service disruption.
trechos: Google is committed to preventing future recurrence, and we are taking the following actions:
Improve the API to push changes to global and local network controllers during a service disruption.

acoes.texto: In progress: improve failure domain configuration validation to reject unintended configuration.
trechos: Google is committed to preventing future recurrence, and we are taking the following actions:
Improve failure domain configuration validation to reject unintended configuration.

acoes.texto: In progress: improve the features and testing of emergency tools across different scenarios at regular intervals, and invest in test environments that allow this without impact.
trechos: Google is committed to preventing future recurrence, and we are taking the following actions:
Improve the feature and testing of emergency tools across different scenarios at regular intervals, and invest in test environments that enable us to do this without impact.

Google Cloud Networking experienced reduced capacity for lower priority traffic such as batch, streaming and transfer operations from 19:30 US/Pacific on Thursday, 14 July 2022, through 15:02 US/Pacific on Friday, 15 July 2022.
Duration: 19 hours, 32 minutes

observacoes: The full incident report (27 Jul 2022) and the preliminary Mini-IR (18 Jul 2022) both give 19:30 on 14 July to 15:02 on 15 July US/Pacific (19 hours 32 minutes). The detailed impact section gives other windows: Cloud Networking reduced capacity starting 02:24 on 15 July with the most severe impact from 03:58 to 12:40; GCS impact between 21:57 on 14 July and 12:40 on 15 July; a status update says the GCS issue was resolved as of 15:26. GCS disruption affected 0.007% of GCS requests. The report notes that additional services may have been impacted without meeting the reporting thresholds.
